events.summary: H1 (capacity saturation: ~4x login-surge overwhelms auth-service with autoscaler capped at maxReplicas 8) is adequately proven. Every hop of its causal chain rests on verified findings with tight temporal ordering: surge ~06:50Z (F13/F21), CPU pinned 96.6-98.9% while memory stays 50-57% (F12, CPU-bound), worker pool 64/64 with queue up to ~98k at 06:54:53Z (F10/F11), autoscaler desiring 14 vs maxReplicas 8 (F10/F11), first accept-queue 503 at 06:55:42Z (F9), p99 step pinned 06:51->06:53 (F8), rate-limiting onset in the identical 06:52->06:54 bucket (F36) and sustained ~900/min for ~2h (F39). The one competing hypothesis naming a distinct origin (H2, portfolio-service v4.4.0) is affirmatively contradicted on every testable leg — no declared call edge to auth-service (F46/F47), no deploy/config near onset (F48/F49), no flood/retry signature (F44), no precedent (F50) — failing only a magnitude check that no tool could ever run (portfolio-service has no metric-query interface; permanently unobtainable, not unrun). H3 and H4 are properly contradicted (F1, F2, F4, F10, F12, F14); H5 is largely settled by five flat resource series with coincident-or-later onsets (F16, F24-F26, F17/F18/F19). The residual gap — whether the surge is broad-external vs a single abusive caller — is a secondary detail the hypothesis itself carries as an assumption; it does not change the capacity-saturation mechanism or the immediate remedy (raise the replica ceiling / shed load), so it warrants a confidence cap and an explicit assumption rather than a continued investigation. The maxReplicas=8 'pre-existing' sub-claim rests on absence of a config record with no readable HPA scope (F30); this likewise affects only the remedy framing, not the category or mechanism.

H5 is now largely settled by round-2 data: redis memory/evictions/connected_clients and user-db cpu/disk all flat with no onset (F16, F24, F25, F26), user-db connection rise coincides with the surge rather than preceding it (F17/F18/F19). The one remaining blocking issue is the ORIGIN of the surge: H2 (portfolio-service v4.4.0 driving logins) names a different origin and hence a different fix, and its central hop is untested (automated check flags it; F5 shows no portfolio-service->auth edge, F22 shows the ingress rises above the gateway, but neither excludes portfolio-service being a large share of gateway ingress or a client-re-login trigger). F23/GAPS show no caller dimension exists in metrics, so only gateway request-level logs/traces can settle it. That is obtainable, narrow, and decisive, so I do not accept yet. If gateway access logs show no portfolio-service/single-caller concentration, H1 stands at a high confidence; if they do, H2 leads.

challenges.issue: Assumption 'surge originates outside auth-service's own request-handling code' is supported only by inference (F22 shows ingress rising above the gateway->auth edge). A retry/self-amplifying loop in an upstream caller, or portfolio-service v4.4.0 driving logins, would produce the same signature but is a DIFFERENT origin and remedy. H1 is the ranking leader on a partly untested premise.

The 'maxReplicas=8 is pre-existing, not recently lowered' premise is inferred from absence: F28/F29/F34 cover per-service config only, and F30/GAPS confirm no node-pool/cluster or HPA scope is readable. T5 partially confirmed this; the residual uncertainty should be carried as an explicit assumption and caps confidence rather than being stated as established.

Central hop 'portfolio-service issues mass login/auth calls' is entirely untested; F5 lists auth-service's declared edges as user-db, redis-cache, kyc-provider, api-gateway only, and F33 shows no rollback. Until gateway request-level data either shows or excludes a portfolio-service/single-caller concentration at 06:50Z, H2 cannot be ranked below H1 with confidence — it names a different origin.

All retrieved resource series for redis-cache and user-db are flat with no onset at/before 06:50 (F16, F24, F25, F26), so H5's mechanism is well contradicted; only user-db replication_lag_ms and kyc-provider (has_telemetry=false) remain unobserved. This is a lower-confidence secondary detail, not an open origin competing with H1, so it warrants a confidence cap rather than further tool spend.

The 06:50Z surge is confirmed as arrivals at both auth-service and upstream gateway, but nothing establishes that it is legitimate traffic rather than a bot/abuse ramp; if it is abusive, 'capacity_saturation' is still the proximate mechanism but the remedy differs (rate limiting). Note auth-service exposes rate_limited_per_min (F23) which was never retrieved — a cheap check that could distinguish a throttled bot ramp from organic growth.

Metrics expose no caller dimension (F23), so only request-level gateway logs/traces can settle it.

Does rate_limited_per_min show a rise at/around 06:50Z (indicating the surge is concentrated/abusive enough to trip throttling) or stay flat (indicating broadly spread organic load)? Also report whether api-gateway error_rate rises with the same onset, confirming the gateway is not itself the failing component.
evidence_requests.rationale: rate_limited_per_min is an already-exposed metric (F23) that was never retrieved; it is a cheap, independent discriminator between an abusive/single-source ramp and a broad load increase, and api-gateway error_rate completes the upstream-inheritance claim of F15/F22.

evidence_requests.question: Check whether portfolio-service v4.4.0 (dep-5803, live since 05:50Z) declares or exercised a call edge to auth-service, and whether portfolio-service's own request_rate/traffic rose at 06:50Z. Specifically: what is portfolio-service's request_rate over 06:00-08:00Z, and is it ~zero-to-small (excluding it as a driver of a +3.9k req/s gateway surge) or does it step at 06:50Z?
evidence_requests.rationale: If portfolio-service's traffic is small and unchanged at onset, H2's mechanism is excluded by magnitude and H1 is materially strengthened; if it steps at 06:50Z, H2 becomes the leading hypothesis. F5 already shows no declared portfolio-service->auth call edge; this quantifies the magnitude test with the one tool that owns deployment/dependency data.

critiques.summary: H1 (capacity saturation: ~4x login-surge overwhelms auth-service with autoscaler capped at maxReplicas 8) is adequately proven. Every hop of its causal chain rests on verified findings with tight temporal ordering: surge ~06:50Z (F13/F21), CPU pinned 96.6-98.9% while memory stays 50-57% (F12, CPU-bound), worker pool 64/64 with queue up to ~98k at 06:54:53Z (F10/F11), autoscaler desiring 14 vs maxReplicas 8 (F10/F11), first accept-queue 503 at 06:55:42Z (F9), p99 step pinned 06:51->06:53 (F8), rate-limiting onset in the identical 06:52->06:54 bucket (F36) and sustained ~900/min for ~2h (F39). The one competing hypothesis naming a distinct origin (H2, portfolio-service v4.4.0) is affirmatively contradicted on every testable leg — no declared call edge to auth-service (F46/F47), no deploy/config near onset (F48/F49), no flood/retry signature (F44), no precedent (F50) — failing only a magnitude check that no tool could ever run (portfolio-service has no metric-query interface; permanently unobtainable, not unrun). H3 and H4 are properly contradicted (F1, F2, F4, F10, F12, F14); H5 is largely settled by five flat resource series with coincident-or-later onsets (F16, F24-F26, F17/F18/F19). The residual gap — whether the surge is broad-external vs a single abusive caller — is a secondary detail the hypothesis itself carries as an assumption; it does not change the capacity-saturation mechanism or the immediate remedy (raise the replica ceiling / shed load), so it warrants a confidence cap and an explicit assumption rather than a continued investigation. The maxReplicas=8 'pre-existing' sub-claim rests on absence of a config record with no readable HPA scope (F30); this likewise affects only the remedy framing, not the category or mechanism.

challenges.issue: The 'maxReplicas=8 is a pre-existing ceiling' claim is inferred from absence: no HPA/cluster-scoped config is readable (F30), so 'no recent reduction' is not proven, only unobserved. Minor, since it does not change the category or the immediate remedy.

The origin of the ~4x surge (broad external ramp vs single abusive/bot caller vs upstream retry loop) is undecidable: no caller/client/user-agent dimension exists in any metric (F23) and gateway/auth logs carry no per-request identifier (F41/F42/F43/F45). This is a permanent telemetry limitation, not a missed query; it affects which mitigation (policing vs capacity) is ideal but not the established mechanism.

Its sole untested leg (portfolio-service request_rate magnitude) was never retrievable because no metric-query tool exists for that service; the magnitude-based exclusion is therefore unconfirmed — but every other testable leg (no call edge F46/F47, no deploy/config F48/F49, no flood signature F44, no precedent F50) is affirmatively contradicted, so this cannot promote H2.

user-db replication_lag_ms and the telemetry-less kyc-provider remain unobserved, so two dependency legs of H5 are untested rather than excluded. Minor: no other dependency leg shows any pre-onset anomaly (F16, F24-F26, F17/F18/F19), and neither unobserved leg precedes the 06:51-06:53 step.
